**Elena Rybakina Claims Wimbledon Women’s Title, Jabeur Makes History**

*London, 14 July 2024* – In a tournament that delivered drama, breakthrough performances and historic milestones, Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan lifted the WTA Wimbledon trophy after a hard‑fought three‑set final against Tunisia’s Ons Jabeur. The match, which ended 6‑4, 3‑6, 6‑3, was a showcase of Rybakina’s composure under pressure and Jabeur’s relentless pursuit of a first‑ever Grand Slam title.

### A Final for the Record Books

Jabeur’s journey to the final was a story in itself. The 27‑year‑old, who entered the tournament as a 12th‑seed, became the first Arab woman to reach a Wimbledon singles final. Her run included a memorable three‑set quarter‑final against Czech player Markéta Bouzkova, where she battled back from a set down to win 6‑4, 3‑6, 7‑5. In the semi‑final, Jabeur faced Germany’s Anett Hofmann, winning 6‑2, 6‑4 to set up the historic clash with Rybakina.

### Rybakina’s Path to Glory

Rybakina’s performance throughout the tournament was a testament to her growing dominance on grass. After a straight‑sets victory over world No. 1 Iga Świątek in the quarter‑finals, she faced Romanian veteran Simona Halep in the semi‑final. Rybakina dispatched Halep 6‑3, 6‑4, a result that underscored her rising status as a future Grand Slam contender.

The final itself was a seesaw battle. Rybakina took the first set 6‑4, but Jabeur fought back to claim the second 6‑3. In the decisive third set, Rybakina’s powerful serve and aggressive baseline play proved decisive, as she broke Jabeur’s serve twice to seal the championship.

### Other Notable Matches

The tournament’s quarter‑finals were a showcase of depth in the women’s game. In addition to Jabeur’s clash with Bouzkova, the match between Germany’s Maria Sakkari and Germany’s Nina Niemeyer was a tense three‑set affair that ended 7‑5, 4‑6, 6‑4 in favor of Sakkari. These matches highlighted the high level of competition and the fine margins that separate the top players on grass.

### Reactions

Rybakina, who is 23, expressed humility after the win. “It’s a dream to win Wimbledon,” she said. “I’ve worked hard all season, and today I felt everything coming together.” Jabeur, meanwhile, praised her opponent’s skill. “Elena is a fantastic player,” she said. “I’m proud to have reached the final and to have played a great match.”

### Looking Ahead

With this victory, Rybakina has cemented her place among the elite of women’s tennis and will enter the next season with a Grand Slam title to her name. Jabeur’s historic run will inspire a new generation of Arab athletes, while the tournament’s competitive spirit continues to elevate the sport.

The 2024 Wimbledon Championships will be remembered not only for Rybakina’s triumph but also for the historic milestones and thrilling matches that defined the event.
